delay tip dbdc:
New sessions are shared across links that are up and have an address. The share takes the earliest slots by number, at most 6. A later slot stays out while those earlier slots are already full, even when it is faster. dbdc2..dbdc6 look only at the first N slots; the share is still at most 6 links.
Select 0 to turn the delay rule off: every link chosen above stays in the share.
When it is on, the last <Delay Statistics> samples are averaged to decide who stays. A link still waiting for its first probe (not yet communicating) stays out, the same as a link still coming up. A failed probe uses <Failed Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is (boundary + difference) × 2. A link that has fallen back to Receive Count stays in, and uses <Receive Count Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary. When availability check is off, the link uses <No Availability Check Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary. A link left out of the share stays up; new sessions no longer use it.
1. <Delay Boundary(ms)> is 0:
	Keep a link when its average exceeds the fastest by no more than <Delay Difference(ms)>.
2. <Delay Difference(ms)> is 0 (boundary is not 0):
	Trim only when this group has averages both at or under the boundary and over it. Otherwise the whole group stays.
	After trimming, keep links whose average is not over the boundary.
3. Both boundary and difference are not 0:
	Trim only when this group has averages both at or under the boundary and over it. Otherwise the whole group stays.
	After trimming, keep:
		- Links whose average is not over the boundary
		- Links whose average is over the boundary, but exceeds the fastest by no more than the difference
An average equal to the boundary counts as within it, on the same side as other links within the boundary. Together with a link over the boundary, that starts the trim, and the link on the boundary stays. A gap equal to the difference does not drop a link.
delay tip hot:
Among links that are up and have an address, the default follows the average of the last <Delay Statistics> delay samples (select 0 to turn delay switching off: the smallest slot number wins, and a smaller slot takes over when it comes up).
A link still waiting for its first probe (not yet communicating) stays out, the same as a link still coming up. A failed probe uses <Failed Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is (boundary + difference) × 2. A link that has fallen back to Receive Count stays in, and uses <Receive Count Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary. When availability check is off, the link uses <No Availability Check Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary.
Switch rules:
	1. Among links whose average is within <Delay Boundary(ms)>, use the smallest slot. When the current default is also within that range but has a larger slot, move to the smaller slot this round.
	2. When the current average is over the boundary, stay. Move to the smallest slot from rule 1 only when the current average exceeds that link by more than <Delay Difference(ms)>. A difference of 0 means any excess is enough to move.
	3. When every online average is over the boundary, use the smallest online slot. A boundary of 0 puts every measured delay over the line, so the smallest online slot is used. A link that is not yet communicating is not a candidate this round. <Receive Count Delay (ms)> left empty follows the boundary.
	4. When the current uplink goes down, move this round by the rules above.
An average equal to the boundary counts as within it. Over the boundary is the other side. A gap equal to the difference does not move.
delay tip lazy:
Links that are up and have an address are compared (select 0 to turn delay switching off: while the current uplink stays up it remains the default, even after a smaller slot comes up; when it goes down, the default moves to the smallest online slot).
A link still waiting for its first probe (not yet communicating) stays out, the same as a link still coming up. A failed probe uses <Failed Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is (boundary + difference) × 2. A link that has fallen back to Receive Count stays in, and uses <Receive Count Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary. When availability check is off, the link uses <No Availability Check Delay (ms)>; left empty, that score is the boundary.
When the current uplink goes down, move this round. With delay statistics on, the target is the online link with the lowest average.
While the current uplink is up, its latest sample is checked first. Boundary above 0 and the latest sample still within the boundary: keep this uplink. Boundary 0 and the latest sample still within the difference: keep this uplink. Compare averages when the latest sample is past that line, when there is no sample yet, or when this probe failed:
1. <Delay Boundary(ms)> is 0:
	Move when the current average exceeds the fastest link by more than <Delay Difference(ms)>. The target is the online link with the lowest average.
2. <Delay Difference(ms)> is 0 (boundary is not 0):
	Move when some link is at or under the boundary and the current average is over it. The target is the online link with the lowest average.
3. Both boundary and difference are not 0:
	Move when all of the following are true. The target is the online link with the lowest average
		- Some link is at or under the boundary
		- The current average is over the boundary
		- The current average exceeds the fastest link by more than the difference
An average equal to the boundary counts as within it. Over the boundary is the other side. A gap equal to the difference does not move.
sticky tip: When the default switches among online extern connections, LAN sessions stay on the extern connection they started on. New sessions follow the new default.
